narrative.overview:
A ledger is where a careful person writes down what they hold and what it is worth. This tool is that ledger for the TI compendium: the reader brings the emblems they rolled and the players they are weighing, and the page writes back a figure with its margin of error beside it. The compendium's own world - its banners, the three emblem weaves, the stage - supplies the identity. The ledger supplies the discipline: neutral paper, exact figures, nothing printed that was not measured.

The surface is deliberately quiet so that two things can be loud: the projected figure, and the colour of an emblem. Everything else is greyscale shadcn chrome on Inter. Controls are tactile in the game's sense - chips and cards that read as items you pick up and place, with a clear press, a clear selected state and the emblem's weave arriving when you touch it.

The system is a refinement of what ships, not a new world. Keep the neutral shell, the two-family type pairing and the weave palette; improve hierarchy, first-visit clarity and the physical feel of selection.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral, zero-chroma paper and ink; colour is reserved for emblems and alarms.
Figures first: large tabular numerals, interval directly under the figure.
Emblem colour is a woven pattern measured off the client, never a flat fill.
Tactile controls: a visible press, a visible selected state, weave on touch.
Light and dark are equals; each palette is tuned for its own page.

rules.name: The Four Inks Rule
rules.body: Hue appears only as an emblem colour, an alarm, or the answer's gold. A new accent, a coloured heading or another tinted card is a further meaning for colour, and a reader will look for what it means. Gold is never used on an input, a button or a heading: it marks the answer and nothing else.

rules.name: The One Recipe Rule
rules.body: Emblem colours differ by hue and weave only. Never tune one hue's lightness or chroma on its own; `client/scripts/check-tone.mjs` fails the build when gamut or AA contrast breaks.

rules.name: The Weave Is Not The Signal Rule
rules.body: The colour word ("RED") is always printed; the weave confirms it. Colour is never the only way to tell two emblems apart.

rules.name: The Names In Inter Rule
rules.body: Player and team names go in Inter, never Space Grotesk: it lacks Cyrillic and Greek, and a nickname would render in two fonts.

rules.name: The Tight Scale Rule
rules.body: Steps between type roles are about 1.125, as product UI wants, not the 1.25 a landing page would use. The detector's `flat-type-hierarchy` warning is a known, accepted exception here; hierarchy comes from weight, the Figure size and placement, not from bigger headings.

rules.name: The Interval Sits Under The Figure Rule
rules.body: A projection is set as figure, then caption interval directly below. Never split them across a column or a fold.

rules.name: The Gold Answer Rule
rules.body: The cards that ARE the answer (the lead unit on the banner tab, the roster total on the roster tab) are filled in compendium gold, with no outline. Everything else keeps the neutral 10% ring, including the three slot cards: they are the parts the total is made of, not the output. Gold is how a reader finds the result first; spend it on nothing else.

rules.name: The Lift Means Picked Rule
rules.body: A shadow on an in-page control means it is selected or pressed. Do not use shadow for decoration.

dos: **Do** set every projection as Figure with its interval caption directly beneath it.
**Do** keep colour to the three emblem weaves, Alarm Red and the answer gold.
**Do** give every selectable thing a visible press (1px) and a selected state beyond colour (border, fill, weight).
**Do** run `npm run check:tone` after touching any emblem token.
**Do** keep prose blocks at or under 75ch (about 30rem at 14px).
donts: **Don't** show a placeholder figure; use the skeleton panel.
**Don't** introduce another accent hue, gradient text, or tint any card that is not the answer.
**Don't** fill an emblem chip with a flat colour; it wears the weave.
**Don't** set player or team names in Space Grotesk.
**Don't** use shadows on resting in-page surfaces.
**Don't** explain a thing twice on one screen. Each sentence says one fact once; reasoning lives in the FAQ, not under the number.
**Don't** put a card around a line of three facts.
